notes: Final code measured sequentially in alternating before/after order, three fresh Chrome profiles per side; 1440x1000 viewport, first-card MutationObserver, CDP CPU checkpoint polled every 100ms.

Both scratch servers started from independent copies of the same saved snapshot. Explicit DB_PATH, isolated HOME/TASKS_HOME/HARNESS_HOME/PROCESS_DIR/TMPDIR, PROBE=1, TASKS_EFFECTS=daemon, TASKS_SYNC=off, TASKS_EMBED=0, shared explicit DENO_DIR.
Settled means 15s after first card, then wire quiet and browser addressed subscription apply readiness. Bytes are inbound uncompressed UTF-8 WebSocket payloads, not HTTP or physical network bytes.
Fresh browser identities and clock-sensitive maintenance explain small count/byte drift. Each server kept its copy between samples, just as the historical probe did.

Earlier iterations were measured under high host load (load average ~11); retained as exploratory summaries, not mixed into the final-code samples. Both baseline and candidate timing improved once load subsided (~6). Do not attribute that change to code.

The 479778-byte / 297-ID historical cold target is not attained. T-37383 also recorded a pre-archetype cold payload of 622613 bytes / 549 IDs; the final lazy path is close to that, with on-demand projected descriptors and later graph state.

All final browser samples have 11 cards, 11 Card_Scroll bodies, zero Loading indicators, and zero browser exceptions. TUI boot rendered the board and exited with q (status 0). Probe processes, databases, temporary worktree and profiles were removed.
